analysis.title: Weekly Fund Flows: Strong Equities, Softer Money Markets
key_insights: Global equity funds took in +$98bn in the week ending November 11, up from +$89bn the previous week. DM inflows were driven mainly by US funds, and EM inflows were broadly supported.
Technology funds again saw the largest sector inflows (+$13.2bn on the week, +$68.5bn over four weeks). Utilities funds saw the largest outflows (-$1.4bn on the week, -$6.3bn over four weeks).
US equity funds drew +$63.6bn on the week against +$31.7bn the week before and +$14.9bn the week before that. Four-week US inflows total +$116.8bn.
Global fixed income flows were subdued at +$0.3bn on the week against +$11.8bn the prior week. Long-duration bond funds saw outflows and short-duration bond funds saw inflows.
EM bond funds saw outflows in both hard-currency and local-currency funds, with the EM fixed income total at -$1.5bn on the week.

Money market fund assets fell by -$18bn on the week after +$140.4bn the prior week. GS rates strategists attribute softer money fund AUM growth this year to firm risk asset returns and higher yields further out the curve.
Cross-border FX flows were positive at +$31.8bn on the week, with USD seeing the strongest net demand (+$20.1bn).
Mainland China equity funds took in +$79.4bn over four weeks but only +$2.1bn in the latest week, after +$34.5bn the week before.

Taiwan (+$5.8bn) and Korea (+$4.0bn) equity funds saw continued inflows on the week. Japan equity funds took in +$4.2bn, and Western Europe equity funds saw +$0.4bn after outflows in the prior three weeks.
UK-dedicated equity funds saw outflows for a fourth consecutive week in the table (-$0.8bn on the week). Brazil equity funds saw -$0.4bn.
vol_and_positioning: Equity fund flows over four weeks total +$299.3bn (0.24% of AUM, z-score 4.62), with the latest week at 0.31% of AUM.
Low beta sector funds (consumer goods, real estate, utilities) saw -$7.1bn over four weeks. High beta sector funds (commodity, financials, industrials) saw -$1.1bn.
Money market fund flows are +$154.7bn over four weeks (0.34% of AUM), with the latest week at -0.16% of AUM.
